articles.title: Who is Luis Antonio Tagle, the first Filipino and Asian Dean of Cardinals?
articles.summary: Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle has become the first Filipino and Asian to serve as Dean of the College of Cardinals.

blocks.text: Published October 11, 2026 1:54am
Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle has become the first Filipino and Asian to serve as Dean of the College of Cardinals.
Born in 1957 into a working-class family near Manila, Tagle was ordained a priest in 1982. He later served as Bishop of Imus in Cavite before becoming the 32nd Archbishop of Manila.
In 2012, Pope Benedict XVI appointed him cardinal.

A fluent English speaker and a prominent Catholic theologian, Tagle was considered a possible papal contender in the 2013 conclave that elected Pope Francis and the 2025 conclave that elected Pope Leo XIV.

Beyond his pastoral duties, Tagle has held academic positions at the Loyola School of Theology at Ateneo de Manila University and the Divine Word Seminary in Tagaytay, which is run by the Society of the Divine Word.

He has also served on the International Theological Commission and other Vatican bodies, earning recognition as one of the Catholic Church's leading theologians. He obtained a doctorate in sacred theology from The Catholic University of America in 1991.
From 2015 to 2022, Tagle served as president of Caritas Internationalis, a global confederation of Catholic charitable organizations.

Tagle's close association with Pope Francis led to another major appointment in 2019, when the late pontiff named him prefect of the Congregation for the Evangelization of Peoples, a key Vatican department responsible for missionary work.
In 2022, however, Pope Francis replaced Tagle and the department's leadership following a Vatican-ordered review that identified deficiencies in management and procedures.

Following a reform of the department, Pope Francis appointed Tagle pro-prefect of the section for First Evangelization and New Particular Churches in 2022. The role involved overseeing matters concerning missionary territories and newly established local churches.
On October 8, 2026, Pope Leo XIV approved Tagle's election as Dean of the College of Cardinals following the acceptance of the resignation of Italian Cardinal Giovanni Battista Re.
What is the College of Cardinals?
The College of Cardinals is composed of senior church leaders who advise the Pope and take part in the election of his successor when the papacy becomes vacant.
Under Church law, only cardinals who meet the eligibility requirements may vote in a papal conclave.
What is the role of the Dean?

The Dean serves as the head of the College of Cardinals, coordinating its work and representing the body in an official capacity. The position is often described by the Latin expression primus inter pares, meaning “first among equals.”

The Dean does not govern the Catholic Church in place of the Pope. However, the position takes on particular importance when a Pope dies or resigns, as the Church prepares for the election of a new pontiff.

The Dean presides over meetings of the College of Cardinals and plays a central role in the proceedings surrounding a papal transition. During a conclave, the Dean also invites the elected Pope to accept his election and choose a papal name, provided the Dean is eligible to participate in the conclave. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Trump slams Zelenskyy, says Ukraine should elect new president
articles.summary: President Trump has criticized Volodymyr Zelenskyy for not making a deal with Russia to end the Ukraine war. He has also warned Kyiv against targeting Russian oil refineries.

image.caption: The US president has also warned Kyiv against targeting Russian oil refineriesImage: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump on Saturday said it's time for Ukraine to get a new president, suggesting that current Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not done enough to put an end to Ukraine's war with Russia.
Speaking at the White House, Trump said, "I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal," adding that ”for some reason (Zelenskyy) never does."

Zelenskyy has "lost 30% of your country and you've had over a million people go between the two of them, over 2 million people killed. That's a war that should have never started. And I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president."
The US president also warned Kyiv against targeting Russian oil refineries.
Trump said he had told Zelenskyy to "do what you want" against Russia, but "don't hit refineries."
"He better damn well stop," Trump said.
More to come...

articles.title: 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
articles.summary: Ukraine's leader had said the deal with Russia to release diesel into the US would help Moscow fund the war.

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia.
Zelensky warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war in Ukraine.
Speaking to the media as he left the White House on Saturday, Trump said the Ukrainian president "wants to make problems for the world" by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries.
"He'd better damn well stop," Trump said before suggesting Ukraine should "get a new leader who can make a deal".
Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes, targeting energy-generating and transport facilities, as well as major logistics hubs.
"We said, 'you can do whatever you want to Russia, don't hit the refineries', because that's a world problem that's caused," he said.
"He could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does."
Trump confirmed on Friday that an agreement had been reached with Moscow to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April.
Zelensky reacted by saying the relaxation of the penalties will allow Moscow to raise new funds to source new military equipment to continue the war.
He also accused Moscow of taking the deal "to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they keep dropping bombs on cities" following deadly new strikes on Zaporizhzhia.

On Saturday the EU's foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas echoed Zelensky's criticism, saying suspending sanctions "provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war", adding: "This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won't."
She said European foreign ministers intended to approve the biggest set of sanctions on Russia since the start of its full-scale invasion on Monday.
The deal with Russia is the latest effort from Trump to lower fuel prices in the US ahead of the midterm elections, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war.

That conflict, which began in February, has sent the cost of petrol and in particular diesel skyrocketing, which has soured his standing with the American public who have been stung by the higher pump prices and knock-on effects that led to across-the-board inflation.

articles.title: Joel Villanueva blames 'forces of darkness' behind flood control scam allegations
articles.summary: Senator Joel Villanueva on Sunday recalled the emotional toll of the corruption allegations linking him to the flood control scandal, claiming that political forces had joined forces to destroy his…

blocks.text: Published October 11, 2026 1:21am

Senator Joel Villanueva on Sunday recalled the emotional toll of the corruption allegations linking him to the flood control scandal, claiming that political forces had joined forces to destroy his reputation and hurt his family and religious community.

Speaking before members of the Jesus Is Lord (JIL) Worldwide Church at the Luneta grandstand in Manila, Villanueva recalled how he had to endure "severe criticism and accusations" over the past year, describing the experience as a "painful ordeal" that also affected his family and JIL.
“Yung mga mafia at forces of darkness nagkaisa para ibagsak at yurakan ang aking pagkatao,” Villanueva said, in an apparent reference to the flood control scandal.
(The mafia and forces of darkness joined forces to bring me down and trample on my dignity.)
The senator spoke at the church’s 48th anniversary celebration religious organization founded by his father, evangelist and CIBAC Party-list Representative Brother Eddie Villanueva.

Villanueva also accused political allies of turning against him, saying that in politics, people who had worked together recently could become adversaries and engage in what he described as “black operations.”
“Sa mundo nga po ng pulitika, yung kasama mo kamakailan, sila pa yung gumagawa ng mga black operations against you,” he said.
(Indeed, in politics, those who were with you just recently may be the very same people who would carry out black operations against you.)
Villanueva did not identify who he accused of orchestrating the alleged smear campaign.
He said the allegations became particularly painful when his family and the JIL Church were dragged into the controversy.
“Ang masakit ho sa lahat, pagka ho binabanggit yung pamilya mo; ang pinakamasakit sa lahat, pagka binabanggit yung JIL Church,” he said.
(What hurts the most is when your family is dragged into it; what hurts even more is when the JIL Church is dragged into it.)

The senator, however, urged his audience to draw strength from their faith rather than seek public approval, citing the importance of finding peace and joy in God amid personal and political difficulties.
“The joy of the Lord is our strength,” he added.

Villanueva's remarks came amid investigations into alleged corruption in government flood control projects, in which former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) officials implicated him in alleged budget insertions and kickbacks.
Former Bulacan first district assistant district engineer Brice Hernandez accused Villanueva, who hails from Bocaue town, of benefiting from anomalous flood control projects in the province.
Former Bulacan district engineer Henry Alcantara also linked the senator to alleged kickbacks, claiming that around P150 million was delivered to Villanueva through an aide identified as “Peng.”
Villanueva has denied the allegations.

In September 2025, then Senate Blue Ribbon Committee chairman Panfilo Lacson said documents showed P600 million in proposed flood control projects in Bulacan under the 2023 General Appropriations Act that had been linked to Villanueva by Hernandez.
The Independent Commission for Infrastructure subsequently recommended that criminal charges be filed against Villanueva and other individuals over suspected irregularities in flood control projects.
The commission clarified, however, that its interim report was not a categorical finding of guilt, leaving the determination of criminal liability to the proper authorities.
The Department of Justice later investigated complaints against Villanueva involving alleged ghost flood control projects and the purported receipt of kickbacks.
Villanueva has characterized the allegations as a demolition job and maintained that he has nothing to hide.— GMA News

articles.title: At least 12 killed, hundreds hurt after attack on Riyadh airport: Saudi officials
articles.summary: At least ‌12 ​people were killed ​and 309 others ​were injured in a ‌Saturday attack on King Khalid International ‌Airport in Riyadh, ​the Saudi Civil Aviation Authority said on ​Sunday.

image.caption: Travellers at the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh in April. The oil-rich Gulf has borne the brunt of Iran's attacks in response to U.S.-Israeli strikes that sparked the Middle East war, with Tehran targeting U.S. assets but also civilian infrastructure, including energy facilities and ai

blocks.text: World·Updated
At least ‌12 ​people were killed ​and 309 others ​were injured in a ‌Saturday attack on King Khalid International ‌Airport in Riyadh, ​the Saudi Civil Aviation Authority said on ​Sunday.
Airport had already been attacked twice this week
At least ‌12 ​people were killed ​and 309 others ​were ⁠injured ⁠in a ‌Saturday attack on ⁠King Khalid International ‌Airport in Riyadh, ​the ⁠Saudi ⁠Civil ⁠Aviation Authority ⁠said on ​Sunday.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack, but it comes amid an escalation of missile strikes by Yemen's ​Iran-aligned Houthis against Saudi Arabia.
The airport has already been attacked twice this week, leaving four people dead and others wounded, and badly damaging an aircraft.
Saudi Arabia's early warning system did not ​issue an alert ahead of Saturday's incident.
The Saudi government's media office did not immediately respond to questions ⁠from Reuters.

This image from video, obtained and verified by Reuters, shows thick black smoke and flames rising from a fire at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Thursday. It was attacked again on Saturday. (Reuters)
One of the eyewitnesses reported seeing an explosion and then seeing multiple people lying injured on the ground inside the airport. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport.
An injured traveller told Reuters they saw something fly across the sky outside the airport before part of the ceiling near a departure gate collapsed.
Trump mulls joining war
Following the attack, U.S. President ⁠Donald Trump, speaking to reporters outside the White House, was asked whether the United States planned to join Saudi strikes on the Houthis.
"We may. We're going to look at it," he said. "We just found out about the recent attack. So we'll make a decision. We move very quickly."
The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh said it was "aware of attacks" and "strongly recommends all U.S. citizens avoid this airport and surrounding areas."
The U.K. and Irish embassies in Saudi Arabia said in statements on X that they were also aware of a "serious incident" at the airport.
The Canadian Embassy in Saudi Arabia published a statement advising Canadians to avoid all travel to King Khalid International Airport due to the security situation.
Saudi capital due to hold major summits
Flight-tracking site Flightradar24 showed all flights to Riyadh had either been diverted or cancelled, with only a helicopter hovering over the airport at one point.
Kuwait Airways said it had cancelled flights to and from the Saudi capital due to what it described as the closure of Riyadh's airport because of the "security situation" there.
Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways earlier cancelled multiple flights between their respective hubs and Riyadh, with some cancellations extending into Monday.
How Yemen’s Houthis could supercharge global trade disruptions

Houthi attacks on Thursday and earlier in the week had already prompted a number of carriers to suspend or cancel services to the Saudi capital, shortly before Riyadh is due to host major energy and investment conferences.
Organizers of those conferences said on Saturday they would go ahead as planned, and they sought to reassure attendees of their security.

The Houthis have said airliners should avoid Saudi airspace, declaring it a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against the group earlier this month.
With files from CBC News

articles.title: Anthropic's Claude AI submits a false tip on a Philadelphia unsolved homicide case
articles.summary: An Anthropic artificial intelligence model submitted a false tip to a Philadelphia police website about an unsolved homicide case, authorities and Anthropic said.

image.caption: In a report Friday, Anthropic said one of its Claude models submitted a fake tip about a homicide case to the Philadelphia Polic Department. (Patrick Sison/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
An Anthropic artificial intelligence model submitted a false tip to a Philadelphia police website about an unsolved homicide case, authorities and Anthropic said.
Latest example of AI agents meddling with government websites amid growing calls for regulation

It's the latest example of AI models acting on their own and manipulating government and other websites in ways testers did not intend. In a report Friday, Anthropic also disclosed a separate incident when its AI model submitted forms to an undisclosed government website instead of stopping before submission.
The incident in Philadelphia occurred on July 18 when the AI model Claude Haiku 4.5 was tasked with generating and performing example tasks on randomly selected webpages, Anthropic said.
Claude filled out a form on police site PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com indicating it might have information regarding an unsolved murder listed on the site.

items: OpenAI says its bots have interacted with multiple U.S. government sites in unexpected AI activity
AI agents tried to hack Library and Archives Canada website, research firm says

blocks.text: Philadelphia police said in a statement they were unaware of the incident until Anthropic notified them on Wednesday. Then they found the submission in the website's tip records and confirmed it was marked spam and never forwarded to police.
Latest incident of rogue agents
There are rising concerns about AI companies' unchecked AI agents meddling with everything from U.S. government websites to health-care data. Critics have been calling for more regulation.
In September, another AI company, OpenAI, disclosed six reports of "unexpected or concerning" behaviour in artificial-intelligence models.
OpenAI reveals unexpected AI activity on U.S. government websites

"Unsolved cases involve real victims, grieving families and investigators working to secure answers," the Philadelphia Police Department said in a statement. "Technology companies must take all appropriate steps necessary to prevent their systems from submitting false information to law enforcement."

Anthropic said in its report that most of the reported behaviours are forms of what it calls persistence "in which Claude, when it cannot complete a task as given, works around a restriction instead of stopping."
The company said it was modifying its training to "reduce the likelihood of further misbehaviour."
Anthropic said it briefed the White House on cases that involved U.S. government agencies at the federal, state and local levels, and notified each agency involved.

articles.title: Christa Pike discharged from hospital after surviving execution attempt, attorney says
articles.summary: Christa Pike, who survived Tennessee's attempt to execute her by lethal injection, has been moved back to prison, according to a statement released by her attorneys.

image.caption: Christa Pike is shown on Jan. 12, 2023, in this photo provided by the Tennessee Department of Correction. Her lawyers say she has been discharged from hospital and taken back to prison after surviving an attempted execution by lethal injection on Sept. 30. (Tennessee Department of Correction)

blocks.text: World·New
Christa Pike, who survived Tennessee's attempt to execute her by lethal injection, has been moved back to prison, according to a statement released by her attorneys.
Pike, 50, moved back to Tennessee prison
Pike, 50, was discharged from the hospital and is back at the Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center, the women's prison where she was housed for 30 years, her attorneys said in a statement.

"She is grateful to the first responders and her medical team for their care in these extraordinary circumstances. She is continuing to receive medical care at the prison, and we will continue to track her recovery," her attorneys said in a statement released Saturday.

Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital as the state attempted to execute her by lethal injection on Sept. 30 for the 1995 beating and stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. Pike had been in a hospital since the failed execution.
On Wednesday, a Tennessee judge ordered the state to preserve evidence related to the botched execution, including needles, drug lot numbers and gurney restraints.
Lawyers asking governor to commute sentence

Following the court hearing on Wednesday, her lawyers Luke Ihnen and Randy Spivey said she was awake and speaking after being unconscious and on a ventilator following the failed execution attempt. Her attorneys said her prognosis remains unclear and that she faces a long recovery.
Lawyers for Christa Pike comment on next steps after 'unprecedented botched execution'
Spivey also said Pike was "very aware" that the state tried to execute her and failed, and that she is both "angry and confused."

Ihnen and Spivey said Wednesday's hearing was the first of many of their attempts to gain answers and transparency from the state of Tennessee about what went wrong on Sept. 30 when Pike survived her lethal injection — as well as to have Pike's constitutional rights enforced.
Pike's attorneys said they were continuing to urge Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee to commute her death sentence to life in prison without the possibility of parole.

items: Christa Pike 'angry and confused' after botched lethal injection, her lawyers say

blocks.text: Lee halted further executions statewide following Pike's hospitalization and ordered a "comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred."
The Death Penalty Information Center says Pike is the first person to survive after receiving lethal injection drugs during an execution.
With files from CBC News

articles.title: Marcos disappointed Philippines halted Bataan Nuclear Power Plant
articles.summary: More than four decades after the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant was mothballed, President Marcos expressed disappointment that the facility was halted, as he claimed that people are now concerned about…

blocks.text: October 11, 2026 | 12:00am
President Bongbong Marcos visits the Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Institute (SNRSI) on October 10, 2026.
Photos courtesy of MPC Pool | via Alexis Romero

MANILA, Philippines — More than four decades after the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant was mothballed, President Marcos expressed disappointment that the facility was halted, as he claimed that people are now concerned about having access to affordable electricity, regardless of its source.

During the fourth day of his five-day working visit here, Marcos visited the Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Institute, which was established in 2014 to build up the country’s capabilities in nuclear safety, science and engineering.

Speaking to officials of the institute and business executives yesterday, Marcos said the Philippines already had a pool of nuclear energy experts, but the development of the Bataan power plant was never completed.

“In 1986, we were already in the first two phases. In fact, that pool of trained… professionals, government, (people with) master’s (degrees), PhD, professionals... They’re still around waiting to put their knowledge into practice,” he said.
His father and namesake, the late president Ferdinand Marcos Sr., had ordered the building of the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant to address an oil crisis in the 1970s.
The facility was completed in 1984, but was mothballed in 1986 after the elder Marcos was ousted through the people power revolution.
The Chernobyl nuclear disaster that took place in 1986 intensified opposition against the use of nuclear energy for power generation.
In 2022, former president Rodrigo Duterte approved the inclusion of nuclear power in the Philippines’ energy mix, saying it would close the gap between rising energy demands and supply.

Executive Order 164 issued by Duterte on Feb. 28, 2022 states that the government will tap nuclear power as a viable alternative baseload power source, along with alternative energy sources “to address the projected decline of coal-fired power plants which come under increasing environmental opposition.”

articles.title: Romualdez allowed to sign court order in jail
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan Third Division has granted the request of former speaker Martin Romualdez to sign a court order on Oct. 12 while in detention at the New Quezon City Jail.

blocks.text: October 11, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Third Division has granted the request of former speaker Martin Romualdez to sign a court order on Oct. 12 while in detention at the New Quezon City Jail.
Romualdez had requested permission to be allowed to sign the pre-trial order while he was at the city jail.
The order is issued following a pre-trial conference, during which both the prosecution and defense mark their respective evidence and lay out the facts and issues to be tackled during the trial.
This will serve as a record of matters taken up during the conferences, amendments allowed to the pleadings and agreements or admissions made by the parties.

“The Sandiganbayan Third Division has granted accused Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez’s motion to sign the Pre-trial Order at BJMP (Bureau of Jail Management and Penology) Payatas, Q.C. on Oct. 12, 2026,” the Third Division’s clerk of court, Dennis Pulma, said.
The hearing for Romualdez’s petition for bail will start tomorrow.

Romualdez, along with former lawmaker and now fugitive Zaldy Co and two other individuals, are facing plunder charges for allegedly receiving around P7.4 billion in kickbacks from government projects from 2022 to 2025.

The court also allowed Romualdez to remotely attend the hearings via video conference, provided that he will immediately submit an informed waiver in accordance with the guidelines on the conduct of video conferencing.
In previous proceedings, including his arraignment where he entered a not guilty plea, the former speaker attended through video conference.
The anti-graft court, however, said it may still request the former speaker to appear in person should it become necessary.

articles.title: Senators weigh in on Mark Villar’s majority bloc move
articles.summary: Senators from the majority bloc weighed in on the move of Sen. Mark Villar to bolt the Alan Peter Cayetano-led minority to join them in the ruling coalition in the upper chamber.

blocks.text: October 11, 2026 | 12:00am
Senator Mark Villar on March 2, 2026.
STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Senators from the majority bloc weighed in on the move of Sen. Mark Villar to bolt the Alan Peter Cayetano-led minority to join them in the ruling coalition in the upper chamber.
Speaking to dzMM yesterday, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said he and Villar’s family are good friends, even before their Senate terms.

“As for myself and Mark, we have been friends for a long time; in fact, he is very close to our family. So, we know each other personally. In our discussions, we share the same desire for the Senate to remain stable and for work to proceed smoothly – especially regarding legislation and the measures needed to boost our economy,” Gatchalian said.
The Senate President said Villar moved to join them in the majority because he liked the current leadership’s “direction” and “to bring stability.”
Former senate president Franklin Drilon had a completely different take on the latest shift in political allegiances.
Speaking to dwIZ yesterday, Drilon did not mince his words in saying Villar’s move was indicative of how he would vote in the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
“Let’s be frank. That’s one added vote for conviction,” he said without elaborating.
Amid talk that Villar’s move meant a sure conviction vote, Gatchalian said senator-judges like them have to rely on the evidence presented in rendering their decision.
“It all boils down to the evidence and how the senators weigh that evidence. So, when it comes to the impeachment, the senators are independent in their appreciation of the evidence,” he said.
“The senators will certainly have varying mindsets when it comes to the impeachment,” Gatchalian added.

Villar was a member of the majority before he joined Cayetano in ousting then Senate president Vicente Sotto III last May. He stood by Cayetano when the latter became minority leader after his ouster last June. With Villar’s move to the majority, he leaves behind his sister, Sen. Camille Villar, who remains with the Cayetano bloc.
He made the jump as their family faces preliminary investigation by the ombudsman for graft over residents’ complaints in the water service of the erstwhile Villar-led PrimeWater Infrastructure Corp.
Cayetano has said Villar’s move was meant to appease the administration which wanted to have more allies in the upper chamber.

Amid talk that the next minority senator to jump ship is Sen. Loren Legarda, Sen. Kiko Pangilinan said Legarda is welcome, having been a member of the majority before she aligned herself with Cayetano.
Gatchalian said he wished Legarda well amid reports that her medical leave abroad was for treatment of her serious lung condition.
Legarda’s medical leave abroad coincided with a preliminary plunder investigation on her and her son, Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste, for their role in alleged ghost solar farm projects.
Legarda’s spokesman Tony La Viña has said the senator is open to rejoining the majority amid shifting alliances that is “normal” in the Senate.

articles.title: ICC allows 7 additional incidents in Duterte case
articles.summary: Trial judges of the International Criminal Court have allowed prosecutors to include additional incidents in the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte.

blocks.text: October 11, 2026 | 12:00am
Photos show former president Rodrigo Duterte during his first in-person appearance before the tribunal since his arrest in March 2025.
Photos / ICC | via Janvic Mateo

MANILA, Philippines — Trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) have allowed prosecutors to include additional incidents in the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte.
In its 18-page decision released on Friday, the ICC Trial Chamber III formally allowed the prosecution to increase the number of incidents included in the case from 49 to 56.
The decision did not state what the additional incidents were.
But it denied the inclusion of one incident as it is not within the temporal parameters of the charges previously confirmed by the pre-trial chamber.
The decision stemmed from the two motions filed by Duterte’s legal team questioning the eight additional incidents added by the ICC prosecutor ahead of next month’s trial.
Defense lawyer Peter Haynes argued that the additional incidents “constitute new material facts and therefore fall outside of the facts and circumstances of the case.”
He urged the judges to either direct the prosecution to “re-file” the document to reframe the charges or to order the removal of the eight additional incidents.
The trial chamber denied the first request and partially granted the second motion.
In its decision, the trial chamber said the additional incidents are “all prima facie (and) fall within the factual, geographical and temporal scope of the charges.”
However, it said Incident 57, which was supposed to be included in the charges involving alleged murder of high-value targets, fall outside the confirmed charges “of between July 2016 and July 2017.”
Records show that the said incident occurred “two weeks after” the covered period.

“In the temporal context, the word ‘between’ means during the time period that separates two specific points in time or events. This necessarily connotes a precise interval of time, defined by a beginning and an end point,” read the decision.

“The Chamber finds that, while the term ‘around’ may allow for a greater degree of flexibility in the context of a specific charged event, it would be inappropriate to apply the same degree of flexibility to the charged period in the instant case,” it added.
The judges directed the prosecution to update its list of witnesses, list of evidence and trial brief to reflect the removal of Incident 57.

Duterte is facing three counts of crimes against humanity, divided into alleged killings by the so-called Davao Death Squad (DDS), alleged murders of high-value targets during the drug war and killings during barangay clearance operations.

articles.title: PAF to acquire advanced Black Hawk training systems
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines is acquiring an advanced virtual training and maintenance system from US-based Lockheed Martin for its growing fleet of 31 Black Hawk helicopters.

blocks.text: October 11, 2026 | 12:00am

Lockheed Martin’s S-70 Black Hawk virtual maintenance trainer provides interactive 3D simulations of maintenance tasks and is one of a family of high-fidelity, synthetic training devices currently available
Businessworld / LOCKHEED MARTIN

MANILA, Philippines — The Armed Forces of the Philippines is acquiring an advanced virtual training and maintenance system from US-based Lockheed Martin for its growing fleet of 31 Black Hawk helicopters.
Lockheed Martin announced yesterday its upcoming delivery of helicopter training devices and services that will enable in-country pilot training for the Philippine Air Force (PAF).

The US-based global defense technology company said it has signed a direct commercial sale contract with the Department of National Defense (DND) involving the delivery of S-70 Black Hawk full motion simulator, a virtual maintenance trainer and associated courseware to the PAF.

Lockheed said the Philippines operates a fleet of European-made Sikorsky Black Hawks for a range of missions including search and rescue, humanitarian aid, firefighting and troop transport across the archipelago.

“It’s a privilege to partner with the Philippine Air Force with a suite of systems to support their training requirements as they grow their fleet of S-70 Black Hawk helicopters,” Lockheed Martin vice president for Air and Commercial Solutions Tim James said.

“This contract award is a long term investment in the PAF’s mission readiness and reflects Lockheed?Martin’s proven ability to deliver sustainment solutions across the entire operational pipeline,” he added.
Lockheed Martin said the S-70 Black Hawk full motion simulator is an aircraft digital twin training solution that replicates the exact sights and sensations of flying an S-70 Black Hawk aircraft.

The virtual maintenance trainer delivers high fidelity, physics-based models of every airframe subsystem, from hydraulics to avionics, that lets maintainers train in a fully immersive, risk-free environment.

“Lockheed Martin remains committed to its longstanding partnership with the Philippine Air Force. Through these advanced training systems, we effectively support the needs of its growing force and expanding Black Hawk fleet,” Lockheed Martin vice president and regional chief executive for Asia and India William Blair said.
“These solutions build on the PAF’s ongoing efforts to enhance training, ensuring crews and maintainers remain mission ready, while advancing their broader modernization goals,” he added.
In addition to the training devices and courseware, Lockheed Martin said the contract includes sustainment and spares support through August 2028.
Meanwhile, the PAF will continue to train Black Hawk pilots at the US-based Sikorsky Training Academy as its in-country training capability is being established.

Lockheed Martin, in a statement, said it “uses a digital twin of the Black Hawk to build the most accurate and up-to-date representation of the aircraft’s systems, components and configurations to enhance training effectiveness, and a digital thread of the Black Hawk’s operational flight program to create high fidelity simulations in days rather than years to keep pace with aircraft modernization efforts.”
In addition to the Black Hawk, Lockheed Martin also supports training for other Lockheed Martin aircraft including the CH-53K, F-35, F-16 and C-130J.

articles.title: Recto to agencies: Speed up El Niño spending, procurement
articles.summary: Malacañang has ordered government agencies to accelerate spending and preparations for the expected “Super El Niño,” which could intensify in the coming months and persist…

blocks.text: October 11, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang has ordered government agencies to accelerate spending and preparations for the expected “Super El Niño,” which could intensify in the coming months and persist through the first half of next year.
Preparations for the weather phenomenon and efforts to ensure adequate food and water supplies were discussed during a meeting led by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto on Oct. 8.

Recto assessed the spending performance of government agencies and emphasized the need for early procurement preparations for next year’s programs to ensure projects can begin promptly and contribute to economic growth.

“We have one more quarter to improve spending for the year. Let’s get our acts together in the fourth quarter. Spend and start doing early procurement, especially on programs that would strengthen our response against El Niño. This way, we can fully catch up in the first quarter of next year,” Recto said in a statement.

He urged agencies to sustain the 7.5 percent growth in government disbursements during the first three quarters and maximize the remaining three months of the year by accelerating projects and assistance programs ready for implementation.

Priority programs include interventions to help farmers and fisherfolk prepare for El Niño, such as solar-powered seed cold storage facilities and irrigation systems. Other priorities include education, health, infrastructure and transport procurement, cash assistance and employment support.
“Preparedness is not a reason to panic. It is a reason to act early. Our job is to make sure that when the effects of El Niño come, the government is ready and Filipinos are protected,” Recto said.
He added that he would meet with key local government units to ensure preparations address conditions on the ground.

“El Niño will not affect every area in the same way. The risks and needs of one community may be different from those of another. We need to know where the risks are greatest and make sure our response matches the situation in each area,” he said.

The Department of Agriculture assured the government that rice, meat and vegetable supplies were sufficient. It also reported ongoing measures to protect agricultural production and assist farmers and fisherfolk affected by prolonged dry conditions.
These include production assistance, crop insurance indemnification, livestock support and water supply interventions.
Funding has also been provided for cloud-seeding operations in Cagayan, Central Luzon, Central Visayas, Eastern Visayas and the Negros Island Region.
The administration is likewise promoting climate-resilient investments to sustain food production, including solar-powered irrigation systems and solar-powered seed cold storage facilities.

The Department of Environment and Natural Resources, for its part, is preparing water-allocation strategies, managing reservoir levels and prioritizing household and irrigation needs based on established triggers.
Additional water supply facilities are expected to become available by the end of the year and in the first quarter of 2027, Recto’s office said.

The government also plans to reactivate 59 deep wells and optimize water treatment plants and other facilities in Cavite, Rizal, Laguna and San Mateo. It has placed 135 stationary and 105 mobile water tankers on standby.

The Department of Energy assured the government that the country had adequate power supply and said it was coordinating with generation companies to prevent unplanned outages. It also plans to expedite the grid integration and operationalization of new power plants scheduled for completion before the end of 2026.

Meanwhile, the Department of Health is strengthening surveillance for heat-related and climate-sensitive diseases and preparing essential medicines, medical supplies and water, sanitation and hygiene resources.

The agency is assessing the readiness of hospitals and other health facilities, identifying equipment and resource requirements and coordinating with other agencies to strengthen hospital power resilience and ensure reliable water access, particularly in high-risk areas.
The DOH advised the public to be wary of signs of heat stroke, which can be life threatening.
Symptoms include loss of consciousness, high body temperature, difficulty in breathing, confusion, slurred speech and convulsion. — Rhodina Villanueva

articles.title: Senate court takes break for budget deliberations
articles.summary: Senators will take a break from their duties as impeachment court judges this week so they can focus on deliberating the proposed budget and having it approved before the year ends.

blocks.text: October 11, 2026 | 12:00am
Senator Win Gatchalian on March 6, 2026.
STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Senators will take a break from their duties as impeachment court judges this week so they can focus on deliberating the proposed budget and having it approved before the year ends.

Speaking to radio dzMM yesterday, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian stressed the need for the Senate to go back to discussing the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027 after serving as an impeachment court.

Gatchalian said he expects the prosecution and defense to wrap up their examination of the last prosecution witness – forensic financial analyst and certified public accountant Alexander Cabrera – on Vice President Sara Duterte’s alleged unexplained and undeclared wealth during the next trial dates tomorrow and on Tuesday.
Dedicating the first half of October to the impeachment trial has helped the court expedite the proceedings and make a room for discussion of the national budget by the Senate starting Wednesday.

This week’s schedule was supposed to be dedicated to whole day impeachment trial dates, but Gatchalian said the tail-end of the week would be dedicated to the prosecution’s formal offer of evidence, which is not expected to take much time.
He said trial will resume after the Undas break or on Nov. 9, in time for the defense to present its counter-evidence on all three Articles of Impeachment.

“So I think it’s best to take a pause (from impeachment trial) so we can go back to the budget because we need to sponsor the budget when we return on Nov. 9, because there is a timetable for the budget. Before the end of the year, we have to have it approved. If not, then we’ll have to reenact. And it’s not good to reenact because our economy is not good,” he said.
“So we need to sponsor the budget so we can take it to the plenary. After the plenary, there is bicam. So by Wednesday, we will be holding budget hearings all the way to Nov. 9,” he said.
Trial would also have resumed by then to coincide with budget plenary debates.

Senators will have their hands full in December, their traditional schedule to meet with the House of Representatives for a bicameral conference committee so they could reconcile the conflicting provisions of the 2027 General Appropriations Bill, as well as comply with their target of rendering a fair verdict on Vice President Duterte before the end of the year.
Senator-judges are feeling the pressure of doing their best amid their grueling jobs of hearing the evidence as impeachment judges and studying the national budget proposal, Gatchalian said.

“Our senators and senator-judges are really under pressure because we need quality for their two tasks. We can’t sacrifice the budget for the impeachment and vice versa. We need quality work, quality debate for the impeachment and vice versa – quality debate, quality analysis. That’s the challenge,” he said.

articles.title: Ombudsman, GSIS inspect Jinggoy’s office
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman and the Government Service Insurance System have inspected detained Sen. Jinggoy Estrada’s stripped Senate office, with the former looking into possible legal…

blocks.text: October 11, 2026 | 12:00am
Photos show the condition of the office previously occupied by Senator Jinggoy Estrada at the Senate in Pasay City on October 5, 2026
Ryan Baldemor / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Ombudsman and the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) have inspected detained Sen. Jinggoy Estrada’s stripped Senate office, with the former looking into possible legal violations and the latter checking the structural integrity of the dismantled space, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian confirmed yesterday.

Speaking to radio dzMM, Gatchalian said the Senate is cooperating with the ombudsman, which inspected the office on the sixth floor last Thursday to look into Estrada’s decision to strip the room of its furnishings and fixtures instead of turning it over in usable condition to its next occupant, Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III.

“They did not say what their purpose was. It is obvious, the ombudsman. So my instruction to the secretary was to give them our cooperation and assist them with their needs. And to be truthful and honest with the documents,” Gatchalian said.
The GSIS management also inspected the office a few days ago after seeing photographs of its condition, Gatchalian said.
The Senate rents a portion of the GSIS building.

“The GSIS also came a few days ago when they saw the picture and conducted an inspection. The GSIS is concerned about the structural integrity of the office because the office belongs to them,” he said.

Gatchalian reiterated that turning over a dismantled office was not standard practice, contrary to Estrada’s claim that he was entitled to do so because he had used personal funds to renovate the room.

Estrada’s removal of the office’s furnishings, including the toilet, electrical sockets and wall panels, means Sotto will have to undertake a major renovation, with the government shouldering the cost.

articles.title: Dozens reported injured in Yemeni Houthi attack at Riyadh airport
articles.summary:
Saudi authorities yet to confirm strike as government-allied forces in Yemen claim successful offensive to retake Bab al-Mandab strait

Yemen’s Houthis have launched a missile attack on…
articles.byline: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor and agencies

blocks.text: Yemen’s Houthis have launched a missile attack on Riyadh’s international airport in Saudi Arabia, with dozens reported wounded and a witness describing panic in the terminal.

Saudi authorities did not confirm any new attack or evacuation, but one witness reported hearing an explosion while waiting to board a flight, and another said they saw a strike that left people wounded.
“I was on gate 403,” at the domestic terminal, the witness told Agence France-Presse. “I saw [gate] 401 hit, I saw injured [people] in front of my eyes. Everyone was running.”
A source at a local hospital told the news agency that five people were in intensive care after being wounded at the airport, and “dozens” more had been injured.
The relative of one injured person said they had been wounded in the shoulders and arms by shattered glass and taken to hospital.
Witnesses said people were being evacuated from the airport.

Saturday’s incident comes amid an escalation of missile strikes by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi ⁠on the kingdom. The airport has already been attacked twice this ​week, leaving four people dead and ‌others wounded, and ‌badly damaging an aircraft.
The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government unravelled in July.

The attack came as forces allied to the UN-recognised government in Yemen claim to have mounted a successful offensive to retake the Bab al-Mandab strait from Houthi rebels, but accounts vary as to whether the push has been repelled.

blocks.caption: Fighters from the Southern Giants Brigades clash with Houthis near the Bab al-Mandab strait in Taiz province, 6 October. Photograph: Yemen Giants Brigades Media Centre/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: A Houthi spokesperson said forces from the Saudi-backed government based in Aden “were targeted with a large number of ballistic missiles, artillery support and heavy weapons, resulting in the destruction of more than 22 armoured vehicles and the killing and wounding of dozens, including a number of commanders.
“More than 30 ambulances arrived in Aden to transport the dead and wounded from the Saudi enemy’s mobilisations.”

By contrast, the Saudi ambassador to Yemen, Mohammed al-Jaber, said: “Blessed Friday and victory for every Yemeni and Arab. Bab al-Mandab has been cleared of the remnants of the Houthi terrorist militia.”

blocks.caption: The Southern Giants, linked to the STC, are the chief pro-government force fighting around the Bab al-Mandab strait. Photograph: Yemen Giants Brigades Media Centre/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The exposed 5 sq mile (13 sq km) Perim Island straddles the strait, acting as a lookout point for all traffic from the Red Sea into the Gulf of Aden and towards the Indian Ocean. Aidarous al-Zubaidi, the president of the Southern Transitional Council (STC), one of the main political forces in the south of Yemen, claimed the island and coastal area had been recaptured from Houthi hands.

An official military spokesperson for the UN-recognised government forces qualified the claim, saying only half the area had been recaptured so far. Waddah al-Dabish said newly established Houthi defensive lines had been broken on the land next to the strait, leading to the death of thousands of Houthi fighters.

It is thought that as many as 500 Houthis fighters are stationed on the island, and Saudi Arabia is desperate to be able to report that the strait has been reclaimed to show that the land counteroffensive it launched at the beginning of the week is advancing.

blocks.caption: Southern Giants fighters fire at Houthis near the Bab al-Mandab strait in Taiz province, 6 October. Photograph: Yemen Giants Brigades Media Centre/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The report came as the United Nations’ special envoy to Yemen, Hans Grundberg, admitted to the UN security council in New York that Yemen – the poorest country in the world – had lapsed back into full-scale war and said the first victims would be women and children.

The Houthis seized control of the strait two weeks ago and said no Saudi-linked commercial traffic would be permitted to go through the narrow waterway. The Houthis are waging a war to remove Saudi influence from Yemen, and have been mounting missile attacks on Riyadh in support of this objective.

There have been previous premature reports of military breakthroughs by the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since it launched its counteroffensive at the start of the week, but the recapture of the land by the strait and Perim Island (also known as Mayyun Island) is a military prize western governments desperately need.

articles.title: Thousands gather in London to express support for Palestinians after three years of ‘genocide’
articles.summary:
March is first since Ed Miliband declared UK’s position was that Israel’s occupation of West Bank was unlawful

Thousands of people have gathered in central London to express their support…

blocks.text: Thousands of people have gathered in central London to express their support for Palestinians after three years of “genocide” carried out against them by Israel.

The demonstrators, many wearing keffiyehs and holding Palestine flags, gathered on the Embankment at midday on Saturday. Some carried placards reading “End the genocide” and “Free Palestine“ as they marched towards parliament. A bride and groom appeared to be among those in attendance and a two-minute silence was held to reflect on the lives lost in Gaza.

Protesters were calling for the UK government to stop supplying arms to Israel, which various bodies – including the UN, Amnesty International, B’Tselem and Physicians for Human Rights, the latter two of which are Israeli-based – have said is committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.

A ceasefire was declared a year ago but Israeli airstrikes have continued in Gaza. In the last year, the overall death toll has risen by a further 1,400 people. Settlers have also ramped up their attacks against Palestinians in the West Bank. According to UN figures, 230 Palestinians were killed in the West Bank by Israeli forces and settlers in 2025.

Husam Zomlot, the Palestinian ambassador to the UK, shared a video from the march on social media. “Three years on, Israel’s atrocities in Gaza and the West Bank continue, and so does the solidarity of the British people. Louder, bigger, and not going anywhere. Thank you all,” he said. By Saturday afternoon, organisers said 250,000 people were at the march.

The Metropolitan police have imposed conditions on the event – which is organised by the Palestine Coalition, which has organised more than 30 mass demonstrations since October 2023, with a counter-protest by Stop The Hate – to “minimise the risk of serious disruption to communities”.
The Metropolitan police posted on X saying: “The front of the procession has now entered Whitehall where a rally will take place.
“Several arrests have been made so far including a woman and a man with placards declaring support for proscribed organisation Palestine Action.
“We have also arrested a number of protesters on suspicion of criminal damage after they climbed on to the Battle of Britain memorial on Victoria Embankment.”

The national march is the first held since the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, announced sweeping sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements and declared the UK government would take the official position that Israel’s occupation of the West Bank was unlawful in its entirety. He also told the Commons that settler terrorists supported by Benjamin Netanyahu’s government are committing ethnic cleansing in the West Bank.

At Labour party conference last month, Miliband appeared to reference the marches, which at their peak regularly numbered hundreds and thousands of people, telling the audience in Liverpool: “I want to say to the millions of people in this country and indeed elsewhere who have been moved and outraged by the plight of the Palestinian people: we hear you, you were right.”

Deputy assistant commissioner Carl Galvin said: “We know Saturday’s event, so close to the third anniversary of the terror attack on Israel, has the potential to have a greater impact on communities than the previous national marches.”
Galvin, who is leading the policing operation this weekend, said the force’s presence on Saturday will be “significant”.
“We will also be using powers under the Public Order Act requiring anyone in the protest area wearing face coverings to deliberately conceal their identity to remove them,” Galvin continued.

The Met have imposed conditions on the march and require the group to travel via Westminster Bridge, York Road, Waterloo Bridge and The Strand on to Whitehall, with a rally concluding by 6.30pm. The force has said that any speeches and music must conclude by 5.30pm.
A counter-protest by Stop The Hate is also taking place, with about 30 people gathered outside New Scotland Yard, some with flags.

The force has also imposed conditions on the demonstration “to minimise the risk of serious disruption”. The demonstrators must remain within a designated area outside the Met’s headquarters, with the assembly concluding at 2.30pm.

Last Saturday, on the third anniversary of the 7 October attacks, when Hamas militants broke across the Israeli border to launch a wave of attacks on kibbutzim, border towns, military bases and music festivals, killing at least 1,209 people, a small pro-Palestine student demonstration in central London was held.

The Met publicly appealed to those behind the demonstration to “exercise [their] right to protest on a different date” and admitted that finding the organisers had been “frankly difficult”. In the end, it went ahead and about 100 people attended. Five people were arrested for breaching conditions imposed on the march.
The Palestine Coalition organising the march includes Palestine Solidarity Campaign, Stop the War, CND, the Muslim Association of Britain, Friends of Al Aqsa and the Palestinian Forum in Britain.

articles.title: What to expect at 4th ICC status conference in Rodrigo Duterte's case
articles.summary: PRAGUE, Czechia - The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III will convene the fourth status conference on Tuesday, October 13, to discuss procedural matters before the trial of former…
articles.byline: ANDY PEÑAFUERTE III, JAY-VEE MARASIGAN PANGAN, Reuters

blocks.text: PRAGUE, Czechia – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III will convene the fourth status conference on Tuesday, October 13, to discuss procedural matters before the trial of former President Rodrigo Duterte on crimes against humanity charges.

Trial Chamber III is scheduled to sit from 10 a.m. to 11:30 am local time (5 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. Manila time), with another block from noon to 1:30 p.m. (7 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. Manila time) if more time is needed.
Will Duterte attend the status conference?
According to the ICC Public Affairs Unit, Duterte is expected to be present at the hearing. This will be his third appearance before the court overall.
How can the public watch the conference?
Yes. The ICC will stream the hearing on its website with a 30-minute delay.
The ICC Public Affairs Unit said it will make available the audiovisual links from the hearing afterward.
What would be the daily sitting schedule during the trial?
At the status conference, the judges are expected to discuss how long the Court should sit for opening statements and the first block of evidence in December 2026.

In its October 8 decision, the Chamber adopted a flexible, case-by-case approach, balancing considerations of Duterte’s health with the needs of witnesses, such as those testifying via video link from the Philippines.
The Registry initially proposed the following reduced sitting hours (in local and Manila time):

These sitting hours, alongside a “bloc” schedule (e.g., sitting for three weeks followed by two weeks off), were recommended by the Registry based on the expert panel’s medical examination of Duterte.
What’s the update on the Prosecution’s List of Witnesses?

Trial Chamber III will ask the prosecutors how many witnesses they plan to call and how many hours they expect to need to present their case. The defense and the Common Legal Representatives of Victims will also give their estimates.
Following a judicial ruling on October 9, the Chamber ordered the Prosecution to update its witness list, evidence list, and Trial Brief by October 16 to reflect the formal exclusion of Incident 57.

The Chamber decided on October 2 that for Rule 68(3) witnesses, the Prosecution’s supplementary examination of witness P-1100 was capped at 1 hour, reducing the Prosecution’s requested 2 hours to avoid defeating the purpose of streamlined Rule 68 testimony.
However, the Chamber rejected four associated items that were not adequately explained or used in the witness's statement.
The Defense is expected to present its response to Rule 68 applications and requests for in-court protective measures.

The Chamber previously warned the Prosecution and Defense to conduct rigorous assessments before filing future Rule 68 applications to avoid over-inundating the record with repetitive or minimally relevant material.
Where are the proceedings at now about the disclosure of evidence?
The judges will return to disclosure and the prosecution’s List of Evidence, including recent filings that have raised disputes over how material was reviewed and turned over to the defense.
Based on the Defense’s September 22 motion, the case record currently sits at 62,130 items (over 320,000 pages), with 19,238 listed on the Prosecution's List of Evidence.

The Defense argued that the record is flooded with untriaged, illegible, or duplicate documents, primarily from a 44,400+ item dataset on what it emphasized as “drug-related deaths”. It has asked the Chamber to order a new case record capped at 10,000 items. A decision on this is pending.
However, the Prosecution countered in its October 5 response that the volume is necessary to establish contextual elements of widespread attacks against civilians.
The Prosecution also revealed it had offered a set of agreed facts that would have removed approximately 42,511 items from the case record, but the Defense rejected the proposal.
The Chamber has yet to decide on the Defense’s October 9 request to respond to the relevance and review of the Prosecution’s dataset.

In response to Defense’s arguments that thousands of documents in Tagalog or Cebuano lack English translations, the Prosecution noted that 1,591 of these items were disclosed under Rule 77/exculpatory obligations, which do not require official court translation. The Prosecution also said approximately 130 are silent video clips (such as CCTV footage), and remaining metadata linking issues are being corrected.
Is the Defense ready for the trial?

The Chamber has specifically included the defense’s readiness for trial on the agenda, giving Duterte’s lawyers an opportunity to explain whether they are prepared for the proceedings and whether outstanding issues still affect their preparations.

At the third status conference, the Defense maintained that proceeding with the November 30 trial start date severely prejudices Duterte, given that nearly 57,000 items were disclosed in the final months before trial.
The Defense emphasized the massive time burden required for trial preparation, estimating that reviewing the 62,130 disclosed items would take roughly 16,000 person-hours.

On September 25, the Defense proposed that the Chamber order the Prosecution to liaise with the Registry to create a case record capped at 10,000 items as a compromise to keep the 30 November trial date feasible.
The Chamber reiterated in its October 2 decision that the Defense retains full discretion over how to use its allocated questioning time during trial.
Meanwhile, the Prosecution maintained that the volume of evidence is “reasonable” and that the trial should commence on November 30 as scheduled.
How about the Victims’ Representatives?
The Common Legal Representative for the Victims (CLRV) stated they do not oppose reasonable health accommodations for Duterte, provided they do not prejudice other participants.
The Victims Participation and Reparations Section also highlighted the “strong interest” of victims and affected Philippine communities in following the trial live.
What will the Registry discuss during the status conference?

The Registry is expected to brief the judges on what support it can provide for the trial process. It will also update the court on interpretation arrangements for the start of the trial, an essential practical issue in proceedings involving parties, witnesses, and participants who may use different languages.

In its October 7 filing, the Registry confirmed it can provide an over-ear noise-canceling headset for hearing/interpretation, nursing staff support during breaks, and mobility/seating assistance in court.

If required, the Registry has also prepared protocols to enable Duterte to appear remotely via video link from the ICC Detention Center, complete with dedicated privileged telephone lines for counsel consultation.
Will the public see Duterte in the courtroom during trial?

The Public Information and Outreach Section (PIOS) recommends that the Chamber regularly provide public explanations if Duterte is authorized to leave the courtroom during hearings to mitigate speculation and public concern in the Philippines.
The Registry has ensured that there is no broadcast of Duterte walking into or out of the courtroom. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Christa Pike discharged from hospital and returned to prison, her lawyers say
articles.summary: The convicted murderer was left in a critical condition after she survived two lethal injections.

blocks.text: US death row inmate Christa Pike has been discharged from hospital following her botched execution at the end of last month, her lawyers have said.
The 50-year-old murderer has been returned to the prison where she has spent the last 30 years, according to a statement from her lawyers on Saturday.
She is continuing to receive medical care at the prison.
Pike survived two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbital on 30 September, which left her in a critical condition in hospital.
Earlier this week, she regained consciousness and began speaking - stunning experts, medical staff and her lawyers.
"She is grateful to the first responders and her medical team for their care in these extraordinary circumstances," her lawyers said in their statement.
Pike's case is now in uncharted territory as Pike is believed to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.
Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for low-income young people.

articles.title: Nobel peace laureate says US sanctions on ICC 'unacceptable'
articles.summary: Navi Pillay says the Trump administrations' sweeping penalties on the international tribunal were "unheard of".

blocks.text: Navi Pillay, the winner of this year's Nobel Peace Prize, has called US sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) "unheard of" and "unacceptable".

The South African former ICC judge was awarded the prize on Friday "for her efforts to promote peace and international law", which paved the way for a "more comprehensive global legal order", the Nobel committee said.

US President Donald Trump expressed his disatisfaction with the pick and hours later the US unveiled sweeping sanctions in a significant acceleration of its attempt to "dismantle" what it described as a "rogue" institution.
The ICC said the measures were an assault on the rule of law and the foundations of the international legal order.

Pillay, speaking via video link during an event at the Nobel Peace Center in Oslo on Saturday, said: "There is so much tension and anxiety over the continued existence of international courts, mainly the International Criminal Court in The Hague.
"Most importantly, sanctions have been announced by one country against the judges, just for the judicial orders they issue. This is unheard of, unacceptable."

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio earlier said the sanctions - which include a ban on US entities making transactions with the ICC - were intended to "defend US sovereignty" and accused the court of seeking to prosecute Americans.
The US has already sanctioned 17 ICC judges and officials, but this move sanctions the court itself as an institution and is intended to inhibit its ability to operate financially.

However, the US has provided a six-month grace period before some of these latest sanctions kick in, meaning member states can keep paying for its operations - a move Washington says is to allow countries time to negotiate a "solution to address" US concerns.
The Trump administration claims that the ICC is run by what it calls globalists who threaten American sovereignty.

It is furious over a past investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan the court has since closed and by its arrest warrants for Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The new sanctions, however, do not say that those warrants must be withdrawn before the measures can be lifted.
UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres called the US decision "a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice, of which the ICC is a key pillar".
The UK joined Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan and the Netherlands in saying they "regret and strongly disagree with" the sanctions.
Pillay, 85, also served as UN rights chief, taking part in high-profile work considering allegations of human rights violations, including in Rwanda, Myanmar and Gaza.

Her early work included defending anti-apartheid activists in South Africa, and on Friday she became the country's fifth Peace Prize winner - following in the footsteps of Nelson Mandela and Archbishop Desmond Tutu.

"If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump," she joked after receiving the prize, a reference to last year's winner, Venezuelan opposition figure María Corina Machado, deciding to gift her prize to the US president.
Trump called the announcement of Pillay as 2026's winner "disgraceful and embarassing", and an "indelible stain on the country of Norway".
He has long indicated he thought he should have been awarded the prestigious prize, and was nominated by several allies for it last year.

articles.title: Woman injures three people in third Poland school knife attack in a week
articles.summary: Polish police had already deployed to schools after a female caretaker was killed and several others injured in two earlier attacks in two days.

blocks.text: A woman has been arrested after injuring three people in the third knife attack recorded at schools in Poland this week.
The 21-year-old used a "dangerous object" to attack a 17-year-old girl at an educational institution in the capital Warsaw, police have told news agencies PAP and AP.
It comes a day after thousands of police visited schools across Poland following two stabbing attacks earlier in the week, one of which killed a female caretaker.
A Warsaw police spokesperson said they could not confirm whether the latest incident was related to the two previous attacks.

Authorities told local media that the 17-year-old injured on Saturday had been taken to hospital, but her condition is not life-threatening. Two other women aged 17 and 24, who had come to submit enrolment documents were also injured, the state news agency reported.
Police told local media that the suspected attacker was a student at the school and initial findings suggest she did not know the three victims.

Schools in Poland had been stepping up security following knife attacks at schools across the country on 7 and 8 October. Polish police said they had arrested 76 people after deploying to schools across the country.
"When it comes to the safety of Polish children and peace in our schools, there is no room for compromise," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said ahead of the operation.
Local media, citing a police spokesperson, reported authorities had information to suggest incidents this past week could be related to an internet challenge.
On Wednesday, a 19-year-old student attacked and injured nine people at a vocational school in the central Polish province of Mazovian.
A day later, a 37-year-old caretaker was killed after a 15-year-old entered a primary school in Leszczydół-Nowiny, north of Warsaw.

Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński also said a 17-year-old was detained in the town of Sierpc, north-west of Warsaw, after allegedly stating "on school grounds that he planned to do something... dangerous - that he intended to harm someone".

articles.title: Pulong Duterte questions NBI's move to 'seek his insights' on Gracioso's claims
articles.summary: Davao City Rep. Paolo “Pulong” Duterte questioned why the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) needed his insights if it was confident in the results of the lie detector test administered to former…

blocks.text: Published October 10, 2026 10:54pm

Davao City Rep. Paolo “Pulong” Duterte questioned why the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) needed his insights if it was confident in the lie detector test results administered to former police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr.
Earlier on Saturday, the NBI said it invited Duterte to shed light on Gracioso’s controversial claims, including that he delivered bags of cash to the lawmaker and other family members.
In a Facebook post, Duterte questioned the NBI’s decision to seek his side despite its assessment of Gracioso’s credibility.
“99.9% legit si Gracioso base sa lie detector test ng NBI di ba?” Duterte said.
(Gracioso is 99.9% credible based on the NBI’s lie detector test, right?)

“Aba, kung ganoon pala kayo ka-kumpiyansa sa kanya, bakit kailangan pa ang insights ko? Para saan—may kulang pa ba sa ebidensiya, o kulang lang sa kumpiyansa ang NBI sa sarili nilang assessment?” he added.
(If you are so confident in him, why do you still need my insights? What for—is there something lacking in the evidence, or does the NBI lack confidence in its own assessment?)

NBI Director Melvin Matibag had previously said Gracioso’s claims were 99% truthful based on the polygraph test conducted by the agency. Gracioso has taken at least two lie detector tests, according to the NBI.
If Gracioso’s affidavit was 99.9% credible, the case should stand on its own, Duterte said.
“Hindi naman ako ang nagsabi ng 99.9%. Kayo ang nagsabi niyan. So, put your money where your mouth is. Kung hindi, huwag ninyo akong gawing pampalakas ng loob,” Duterte said.
(I am not the one who said 99.9%. You were the ones who said that. So, put your money where your mouth is. Otherwise, do not use me to boost your confidence.)

Gracioso came forward claiming to have served as a bagman for former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco. He alleged that he delivered money to various political personalities, including several contractors implicated in the flood control corruption scandal.
His claims, however, were disputed by Curlee Discaya, one of the private contractors being linked to the flood control fund mess.—MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Drone strike by Sudan paramilitary kills 41 near Ethiopian border, rights group says
articles.summary: Eight children are said to be among those killed by the strike, which hit a gathering of displaced people.

blocks.text: A drone attack by Sudan's paramilitary forces has killed 41 people in the country's Blue Nile region bordering Ethiopia, a rights group has said.
The strike by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) targeted a camp for displaced people in the state's Abu Shandi area on Friday, Emergency Lawyers said.
The UN Office for the Co-ordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) said it was "appalled by horrifying reports". It said initial reports suggested most of the casualties were women and children.

The Sudanese army and paramilitary forces including the RSF have been locked in a power struggle since 2023, a conflict that has killed hundreds of thousands and displaced more than 14 million from their homes.
It has also created one of the worst humanitarian crises in the world, with millions of people needing medical help.
The army controls much of Sudan's central and eastern regions, while the RSF is headquartered in the western region of Darfur and also controls areas in the south.
Both sides have been accused of using drone attacks.
Ocha said in a statement that the area reportedly struck on Friday had been "under sustained atttack in recent weeks, displacing thousands of civilians and exposing many more to grave harm".

articles.title: Ukraine hit by deadly Russian strikes as ‘thanks’ for Trump diesel deal, Zelenskyy says
articles.summary:
Ukrainian president says money from fuel sales will intensify war as European leaders reiterate support for Kyiv

Russia launched deadly strikes on civilians in Ukraine as “thanks” for a deal…

blocks.text: Russia launched deadly strikes on civilians in Ukraine as “thanks” for a deal cut by Donald Trump with Vladimir Putin to buy large quantities of Russian diesel, Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, accusing Washington of helping fund Moscow’s war.

The Ukrainian president has expressed repeated outrage at the agreement announced by Trump on Friday, which the US president said was needed to reduce diesel prices, and comes ahead of November midterm elections where the cost of fuel is a key voter issue.
The deal, which appeared to blindside Kyiv as it was announced while Ukrainian negotiators were in Miami for peace talks, was described by Zelenskyy as a “gift” to Russia’s president.

He said Russia would use the money it raised from the fuel sales to invest in its war and that “any easing of sanctions” would play into Russia’s hands, “allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer”.

That prediction was realised hours later, when Ukrainian officials announced that a barrage of Russian strikes on the country’s south-east early on Saturday had killed 15 people, including three children.

blocks.caption: Rescuers working at the site of an apartment building damaged by a Russian strike in Zaporizhzhia. Photograph: Reuters

blocks.text: “Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia,” Zelenskyy said on social media on Saturday.

“Last night confirmed once again that in Russia, they take any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they can keep dropping bombs on cities. Different signals are needed,” he said.
There were also “large-scale power outages” in the capital, Kyiv, the country’s largest private energy provider said.

In stark contrast to Zelenskyy’s open frustration with Trump, a Kremlin readout of Friday’s call between the US president and Putin was glowing, with the Russian ⁠news agency Interfax ⁠quoting ​an aide as saying it was “very substantive and friendly”.

“Neither wanted to be the first to hang up,” the Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said of the two leaders. “They hung up simultaneously, literally at the same time.” ​Zelenskyy has previously said Putin is playing games with Trump.

The diesel deal disrupts four years of western financial pressure on Moscow and leaves Kyiv’s allies in Europe and Nato scrambling to adapt their sanctions plan. The EU’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the diesel deal “provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war”.

“This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won’t,” she said on Saturday. “On Monday, EU foreign ministers intend to approve the biggest set of sanctions listings targeting Russia’s war machine since the start of the war.” She was referring to plans to formally add 1,600 new individuals and entities to the EU’s sanctions blacklist.

blocks.caption: Kaja Kallas with Volodymyr Zelenskyy at a summit in Copenhagen last year. Photograph: Piroschka Van De Wouw/Reuters

blocks.text: Major European governments have attempted to balance their diplomatic and trade relationship with a mercurial Trump and their support for Ukraine.

The German government spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said Berlin “remains committed to the sanctions imposed on Russia and is working with its European partners on further sanctions”, adding that support for Ukraine “remains unwavering”.
Ulf Kristersson, the Swedish prime minister, expressed “regret” at the US agreement, saying energy revenues were “a vital source of funding Russia’s war of aggression”.

Zelenskyy said on Saturday that Russia “must feel its losses” and has promised to respond. In the Russian-occupied ‌Luhansk ‌region, Ukrainian attacks in the past 24 hours had killed four ⁠civilians and wounded ⁠five, the region’s ‌Russian-installed governor, Leonid Pasechnik, said ​on Saturday.
Zelenskyy said that Ukraine was ready to take “de-escalatory steps” in the war but only if Russia did the same.
